title: executeSink is the only data endpoint that skips runtime response validation, casting the raw wire body to SinkResponse
description: Every other endpoint in this file pipes the parsed JSON through a runtime guard before returning (loadPipeline -> parsePipelineResponse, previewNode -> parsePreviewNodeResponse, savePipeline -> parseSavePipelineResponse, traceCell -> parseTraceResponse, createSubmodel -> parseSubmodelCreateResponse). executeSink instead does `return post(...)` with no `.then(parseSinkResponse)` and the function signature `Promise<SinkResponse>` forces an unchecked structural cast of whatever `res.json()` returned. There is no parseSinkResponse guard anywhere in src/types/guards.ts, and executeSink is the single data-returning endpoint absent from both client.contract.test.ts (which exercises malformed-200 rejection for the others) and from any response-shape assertion in client.test.ts (its three tests only assert the outgoing request body). This breaks the file's own invariant that backend responses fail loudly at the boundary (per CLAUDE.md: 'code should be allowed to fail loudly... far superior to a fallback which is incorrect and hard to notice'). The downstream consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-48 reads `data.status || 'ok'` and `data.message || 'Written successfully'`, so a malformed/garbage payload is silently masked by `||` fallbacks rather than surfaced — the exact 'incorrect and hard to notice' situation the codebase guards against. Practical blast radius is limited because the consumer only touches two optional string fields with fallbacks, hence not a crash, but row_count/path/format are never validated and any future consumer would trust an unverified shape.
evidence: client.ts:571-580 `return post("/api/pipeline/sink", {...}, { signal, timeout })` with no parse step, vs client.ts:550 `post<unknown>("/api/pipeline/trace", body, ...).then(parseTraceResponse)`. SinkResponse defined types.ts:202-208 (status/message/row_count/path/format). No `parseSinkResponse` symbol exists (grep across frontend). Consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-49 masks with `data.status || 'ok'` / `data.message || 'Written successfully'`.
behavior_preservation: For well-formed backend responses, adding a parseSinkResponse guard returns the same object and is fully behavior-preserving; it only changes behavior for malformed payloads (which currently slip through with silent `||` fallbacks) by making them fail loudly, matching the rest of the client.
